The most important factors that cause the ductility minimum of superalloys are (1) embrittlement of grain boundaries, (2) deformation mechanisms which lead to strain localization, and (3) coarsening of c¢ particles.
A high density of dimples on grain boundary facets (Figure 4(f)) suggests a localization of plastic deformation (void formation and coalescence) to regions very close to grain boundaries.

At room temperature, grain boundary strength is high and the deformation is concentrated in the grain inside. The process of microvoid nucleation and coalescence results in ductile fracture and high ductility.
